worldcombat.skill.speedswap.summary: Exchange your effective speed with the target for a while, flipping who is faster until the window ends and both revert. Pokemon read native speed and speed stages; any other body reads movement speed and the shared speed ladder — one path for all.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.use.0: Borrow speed from a foe that outruns you
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.use.1: Drag a slower foe down to your own tempo
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.use.2: Flip the order when a faster foe opens on you
Cast on a single enemy: the exchange holds %2$s within %1$s blocks and a clear line. Both revert to their original speed stage when the window ends or is cleared.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.mode.exchang: Swap: the two effective speeds trade places — you gain everything if the foe is faster and lose everything if it is slower, symmetric risk; the window is longer (x1.15).
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.mode.dampen: Dampen: both move toward the middle, halving the gap; steady and predictable, with a shorter window (x0.75) and cheaper cooldown (x0.85), but a slower foe drags you down.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.timing: Cast on a single enemy: after %2$s of preparation it spends %4$s PP to swap; the recovery is %3$s, the cooldown %5$s from commit, and the current range %1$s blocks.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.growth.0: At level %1$s the reach grows to %2$s blocks and the window lasts %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.growth.1: At level %1$s the reach grows to %2$s blocks and the window lasts %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.preference.m: Swap: the two effective speeds trade places, symmetric risk, window x1.15. Dampen: both move toward the middle, halving the gap; steady, but a slower foe drags you down (window x0.75, cooldown x0.85).
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.preference.a: The partner only swaps while a threat is this close; smaller keeps it for melee, larger chases out to flip the order.
The speed ratio (foe / self) must reach this before the swap counts as worth it; higher keeps it for genuinely faster foes and avoids pointless back-and-forth.
When on, the partner will also leave its post to swap speeds.
